headline: Record inflows and margin expansion power a standout quarter
summary_short: Revenue rose to $7.08 billion (+31% y/y, +6% q/q) as organic base fee growth, higher performance fees, and HPS Transaction contributions lifted operating income to $2.46 billion (+42% y/y) and diluted EPS to $12.19 (+20% y/y, $13.91 as adjusted).
summary_long: BlackRock's $192 billion of second-quarter net inflows (record $321 billion for H1) pushed AUM to $15.3 trillion, driven by ETFs, private markets, active fixed income, and systematic equity strategies. Revenue growth reflected market beta, 8% organic base fee growth, ~$230 million of HPS Transaction fees, higher performance fees, and 13% growth in technology services/subscription revenue tied to Aladdin adoption. Adjusted operating margin hit 45.9%, the highest in nearly five years, while compensation and sales/asset expense rose alongside higher operating income and AUM. Cash rose q/q on retained earnings; long-term debt was roughly flat. The company raised planned 2026 share repurchases to $2 billion and increased planned quarterly buybacks to $550 million.

drivers.explanation: CEO Fink cited $868B of trailing-twelve-month net inflows, 10% organic base fee growth, and record H1 flows as evidence of accelerating momentum across public markets, private markets, and technology.

Release attributes the 31% y/y increase to positive market impact, organic base fee growth, ~$230M of HPS Transaction fees, higher performance fees, and higher technology services/subscription revenue.

Investment advisory revenue rose on market beta and organic growth; performance fees increased on higher alternative-product and long-only revenue, more than offsetting higher compensation and G&A expense.
The 20% y/y EPS growth reflects higher net income, partly offset by lower nonoperating income and a higher diluted share count versus a year ago.
